text:
alex: Hi team — quick one. I want to add my spouse during open enrollment but theyre not a US citizen and don't have an SSN yet. Their passport + foreign marriage certificate are ready. Can I still enroll them? Any extra docs or tax stuff I should know about?

sara - People Ops: Good question. We can enroll non-US spouses, but we need alternate proof if no SSN. Please upload passport + marriage certificate. If the marriage cert isn't in English, we need a certified translation. For the enrollment record we prefer SSN or ITIN; if you don't have either yet, you can submit "pending" and provide the number within 60 days.

kevin - Benefits Admin: Adding: for medical/dental/vision we can process the dependent without an SSN initially, but some carriers require one later for claims. We'll flag the case with the carrier. If you get an ITIN you can provide that.

alex: Okay. If I enroll now, when would coverage start? Open enrollment technically closes tonight.

sara - People Ops: If you complete the portal enrollment before midnight (open_enroll.redwood.com) the effective date will be the standard plan date (2026-07-01). If you miss the deadline but get an ITIN later, the only paths are a QLE or waiting until next OE. No special exception just for missing OE unless you have a qualifying event.

alex: Understood. What about taxes — will adding a non-US spouse count as a tax dependent / imputed income? Im married filing jointly but spouse lives abroad.

dylan - Payroll: Were not tax advisors but for benefits imputed income rules depend on US tax residency and benefit type. Usually employer-sponsored health coverage for a spouse who is not a US tax dependent can still be offered, but there may be imputed income in some cases (domestic partner vs spouse rules differ). Well route a case to payroll to confirm once Sara uploads the docs. If any imputed income applies it will show up on your payroll notices and well post an explanation.

kevin - Benefits Admin: Also note: some international addresses trigger additional eligibility checks with carriers. We'll ask for spouse DOB and country of residence on the portal form.

alex: Cool. Uploaded passport and marriage cert (English translation attached). Completed enrollment form and marked SSN pending.

hr-bot: Submission received. Case ID: OE-20260715-991. People Ops will review within 2 business days.

sara - People Ops: I see the case. Thanks for the translation. Can you add spouse full name, DOB, and country of residence in a secure portal note so we can pass to the carrier? Also confirm whether spouse will be on the US payroll or is entirely foreign.

alex: Added those details in the secure note. Not on US payroll, lives in UK.

sara - People Ops: Great. We'll submit to carrier for initial enrollment. Kevin/dylan, flagging for carrier special handling and payroll tax check.

dylan - Payroll: Got it — I'll review for imputed income / tax reporting and follow up in this thread once I confirm. If anything is due it will be explained and processed next payroll cycle.

sara - People Ops: Thanks everyone. Alex, well follow up if the carrier requests SSN/ITIN or additional verification. If you get an ITIN before 60 days, upload it to the same case to avoid claim delays. :pray:

alex: Thanks all, appreciate the quick help! :wave:
